name: ATHENA
notes: CERN's ALPHA page: "ALPHA is picking up from where ATHENA left off." The lineage edge predecessor lives on experiment:alpha.

physics_goals.quote: Cold atoms and anti-atoms, such as hydrogen and antihydrogen, could form the basis of a new precise test, as CPT invariance implies that they must have the same spectrum.
physics_goals.value: Compare hydrogen and antihydrogen spectra as a test of CPT invariance by producing cold antihydrogen

summary.plain: A CERN experiment that in 2002 made the first large numbers of cold antihydrogen atoms, by mixing trapped antiprotons and positrons. It ended in 2004; its successor is ALPHA.
summary.technical: ATHENA at the AD: mixed trapped antiprotons and positrons in a cryogenic Penning trap and detected the annihilations of the neutral antihydrogen atoms with an imaging detector. Ran 2000-2004; ALPHA is its successor.
